NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 12 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 29 · 9 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 27, 5:32 PM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 12 DraftKings main slate at 16.1 DraftKings points for $6,600, against Washington. Isaiah Likely (13.2, $5,900) and George Kittle (12.1, $6,500) are next.

Brenton Strange returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.93 projected points per $1,000 at $4,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 27, 5:32 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 12

Trey McBride, ARI vs WAS ($6,600)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 16.1 DraftKings points at $6,600. That is 2.9 points clear of Isaiah Likely. The model gives him 11.1 targets on 33.3 routes. The salary works out to 2.43 projected points per $1,000, 4th of 12 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations McBride averaged 16.0 points with a simulated floor of 3.4 and a ceiling of 41.4, and he holds 15% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 6.5-point underdog at home against Washington, with an implied team total of 17.5 in a game totaled at 41.5.

Isaiah Likely, NYG at IND ($5,900)

Isaiah Likely projects 2nd at the position with 13.2 DraftKings points at $5,900. The model gives him 6.5 targets on 26.6 routes. The salary works out to 2.23 projected points per $1,000, 6th of 12 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Likely averaged 13.2 points with a simulated floor of 2.1 and a ceiling of 37.1, and he holds 12% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Giants are a 5.5-point favorite on the road against Indianapolis, with an implied team total of 23.5 in a game totaled at 41.5.

Value: Brenton Strange, JAX vs TEN ($4,100)

Brenton Strange projects for 12.0 DraftKings points at $4,100, which works out to 2.93 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 12 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 5.3 targets on 19.4 routes. Across 50,000 simulations Strange averaged 12.0 points with a simulated floor of 1.6 and a ceiling of 33.4, and he holds 16% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Jacksonville is a 14-point favorite at home against Tennessee, with an implied team total of 31.25 in a game totaled at 48.5.
